A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeCo study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Content can be matched across table renumbering, relocation, and revised DINOv2 variant names.

before.justification: V2 reports original NeCo results for segmentation, in-context retrieval, multiview correspondence, detection, depth estimation, and ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional comparisons involving original DINOv2, intact-register DINOv2R, and register-removed DINOv2XR.

M1.justification: Section 3 changes the defining training objective from CE(Qt, Qs) + CE(Qs, Qt) to CE(Qt, Qs) alone, substantively revising the specified learning objective. Feature alignment, reference sampling, differentiable sorting, and the EMA teacher remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a correction to the written objective.

E1.justification: The training datasets, evaluation domains, and tasks are retained. Cityscapes, Vaihingen, NYUd depth estimation, COCO detection, and vision-language backbone evaluations already appear in v2. Additional backbone and register configurations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond relabeling existing results as DINOv2XR, v3 adds original DINOv2 and intact-register DINOv2R comparisons in clustering, in-context retrieval, detection, and transfer evaluations (Tables 10–12 and 15). TimeT is removed from the Cityscapes comparison. These changes substantially expand comparisons against the source backbones.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the stated DINOv2 global crop resolution from 224×224 to 518×518, retaining 224×224 for ablations. Table 7a qualifies the previous 25-epoch description with stopping around epoch 7. The Cityscapes evaluation switches retained backbones from ViT-S to ViT-B. These are substantial reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds a targeted investigation of register removal, explicitly motivated in A.1 and supported by comparisons among DINOv2R, DINOv2XR, and original DINOv2. The existing patch-selection, teacher, sorting, ROI-Align, training-duration, computational-control, and qualitative failure-case analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five-seed averaging for subsampled in-context retrieval and overclustering, and best-result selection over ten seeds for community detection. Neither adds confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or a changed repeated-run procedure.

E6.justification: Core results are revised and expanded. Table 2 replaces ViT-B COCO-Things DINOv2R/NeCo scores of 78.3/85.5 with 84.8/86.4; Table 4 also changes extensively. Appendix tables retain earlier results under XR labels and add other variants, including a newly reported ViT-S DINOv2 depth result that worsens from 0.460 to 0.461 RMSE with NeCo. These are revised or additional results under clarified configurations, not established same-setting improvements. Table 5 changes only numerical precision.

T1.justification: The formal definition of the final NeCo loss in Section 3 drops the reverse cross-entropy term. The distance definitions, relaxed-swap mathematics, and sorting-matrix construction in Equations 1–7 remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claimed in-context gains from +5.5%/+6% to +2.3%/+4.2%, and linear-segmentation gains from +7.2%/+5.7% to +1.6%/+4.8%. The proposed contribution, novelty argument, application scope, and broad state-of-the-art claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Table 7 adds an explanation that the best DINOv2R configuration saturates around epoch 7, motivating early stopping; v2 only discusses diminishing gains after 25 epochs in its epoch ablation. The detection discussion also extends its applicability conclusion to the DINO family. Existing patch-retrieval failure mechanisms and broader limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly explains register retention/removal. New Tables 7–8 distinguish five post-training configurations, document configuration-specific GPU hours and stopping information, and map reported experiments to their configurations. This substantially improves implementation traceability beyond v2's shared settings. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Hummingbird, CrIBo, dense self-supervised learning, and unsupervised segmentation remain unchanged. Reference-list differences are citation-page updates caused by pagination.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted revisions to the loss explanation, performance summaries, backbone terminology, and cross-references, and adds configuration explanations. The main narrative, section order, and Appendix A–D organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds configuration Tables 7–8 and expands several appendix result tables. Figure 2 switches from small-model to base-model results, displays Hummingbird instead of TimeT, and changes legends and axis ranges. Figures 1 and 3–7 retain their visual content, with appendix figures and tables relocated through reflow. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves auditability by identifying register-removed checkpoints, adding intact-register comparisons, and mapping experiments to explicit configurations. It also narrows headline performance margins. These gains are limited by unresolved inconsistencies: Table 1 still labels XR baseline values as DINOv2R despite Table 10 distinguishing them, and the main 25-epoch training description is not reconciled with Table 7's early stopping. The revision therefore supports a limited overall quality improvement.
